Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:10:1.english: He is stating the reason of our Tanna - Why they said [that] a minor's find [belongs] to his father.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:10:2.hebrew: וליה לא ס"ל - דמציאת קטן לאביו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:10:2.english: And he himself does not hold [so] - That a minor's found object [belongs] to his father.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:12:1.english: By rabbinic [law] - Because of the ways of peace.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:12:2.hebrew: ונפקא מינה - מדר' יוסי הא אתא לאשמועינן, דהחמירו חכמים בתקנתן כגזל גמור להוציאו בדיינין. וכיון דמדאורייתא לית ליה זכייה, נמצא אביו גוזל את העניים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:12:2.english: And the practical difference - From Rabbi Yosei['s ruling], this is what [Rav Chisda] comes to teach us: that the Sages were stringent in their enactment, [treating it] like full-fledged robbery so as to extract it through judges. And since by Torah law [a minor] has no [power of] acquisition, it turns out that his father is robbing the poor.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:13:1.hebrew: אלא אמר אביי - רבי יוסי נמי כתנא דידן ס"ל דקטן לית ליה זכייה, וגבי לקט היינו טעם: דכיון דיש לו לפועל זה בנים ואשה, עניים עצמן מייאשי מלקט שלה. לפיכך עשאוה כשדה שהלכו בו הנמושות, דתנן (פיאה פ"ח מ"א): מאימתי כל אדם מותרין בלקט? משילכו בו הנמושות — לקוטי בתר לקוטי — דמההיא שעתא מסחו עניים דעתייהו מיניה, והכא נמי מסחו דעתייהו כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:13:1.english: Rather, Abaye said - Rabbi Yosei also holds like our Tanna, that a minor has no power of acquisition. And regarding gleanings [leket], this is the reason [that his son may glean]: since this laborer has sons and a wife, the poor themselves despair of its gleanings. Therefore, [the Sages] rendered it like a field through which the nemoshot have walked, as we learned in a Mishnah (Peah 8:1): From when are all people permitted in gleanings? From when the nemoshot have walked through it — [meaning] gleaners after gleaners — for from that moment the poor divert their minds from it, and here too they divert their minds, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:1:1.hebrew: גבי מתנה דזכות הוא לו זכין לו לאדם שלא בפניו - ושלא מדעתו, דאנן סהדי דניחא ליה שתהא שלוחו. הלכך, כי ליתיה בצד חצרו, דליכא לדמויי לידה דאינה סמוכה לה, תיפוק לה זכייתה משליחותה; כי היכי דשלוחו זוכה לו שלא בפניו, חצרו נמי זוכה לו שלא בפניו. ומיהו גבי מציאה, כי ליתיה גבה דלא נפקא זכייתה משום יד, ליכא לרבויי משליחות; דגבי שליחות איכא דעת השולח או דעת שליח, אבל חצר ליכא לא דעת שולח ולא דעת שליח, הלכך בעינן דעת אחרת מקנה אותו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:1:1.english: With regard to a gift, which is beneficial for him, one may act in a person’s interest in his absence - And without his knowledge, for we are witnesses [that] he is pleased for [his courtyard] to be his agent. Therefore, when he is not alongside his courtyard, so that it cannot be likened to [his] hand since it is not adjacent to it, its [capacity for] acquisition derives from its [status as] agency; just as his agent acquires for him in his absence, his courtyard also acquires for him in his absence. However, with regard to a found object, when he is not near it so that its [capacity for] acquisition does not derive from [the law of] "hand," it cannot be included [under the law of] agency; for with agency there is either the intent of the sender or the intent of the agent, whereas [with] a courtyard there is neither the intent of a sender nor the intent of an agent; therefore, we require the intent of another [person] transferring it [to him].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:3:1.english: [If one] threw a purse - and declared it ownerless for whoever comes first.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:3:2.english: That will not eventually come to rest - within the airspace.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:3:3.hebrew: כמונח דמי - וקנאו בעל הבית הראשון, או לאו כמונח דמי? להכי בעי: אויר שאין סופו לנוח בתוך הבית, כמונח דמי? דאילו אויר שהיה סופו לנוח בתוך הבית, פשיטא לן דאפילו קדם איש אחר וקלטה בתוך האויר, לא קנה, דמשנכנס לאויר קנאו בעל הבית, דתנן במסכת גיטין (דף עט.): היתה עומדת בראש הגג וזרק לה גט, כיון שנכנס לאויר הגג הרי זו מגורשת. הוא למעלה והיא למטה, כיון שיצא מרשות הגג, נמחק או נשרף, הרי זו מגורשת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:3:3.english: [Is it] considered as though it has come to rest - and did the first homeowner acquire it, or is it not considered as though it has come to rest? For this reason [Rava] asks whether airspace [where] it will not eventually come to rest inside the house is considered as though it has come to rest; whereas [regarding] airspace [where] it was destined to come to rest inside the house, it is obvious to us that even if another person stepped in first and caught it in the air, he did not acquire [it], because from the moment it entered the airspace, the homeowner acquired it — as we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Gittin (79a): "[If] she was standing on top of the roof and he threw her a bill of divorce, once it enters the airspace of the roof, she is divorced. [If] he is above and she is below, once it leaves the domain of the roof, [even if] it was erased or burned, she is divorced."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:4:1.hebrew: ואינו מגיען - אלמא מתגלגלים ויוצאין הן ואין סופן לנוח, וקאמר דקנה ליה שדהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:4:1.english: And he does not reach them - Evidently, they are rolling and going out, and are not destined to come to rest [there], yet he says that his field acquires [it] for him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:6:1.hebrew: מציאת בנו ובתו הקטנים כו' - בנו קטן, בגמרא מפרש מ"ט. בתו הקטנה, בכתובות (דף מו:) ילפינן לה מקראי, דקטנה, ואף נערה, כל שבח נעוריה לאביה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:6:1.english: The found item of his minor son and daughter, etc. - [As for] his minor son, in the Gemara it explains what the reason is. [As for] his minor daughter, in Ketubot (46b) we derive it from verses, that [for] a minor, and even a *na'arah* [maiden], all the profit of her youth [belongs] to her father.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:6:2.hebrew: מציאת עבדו ושפחתו הכנענים שלו - שהרי גופו קנוי לו עולמית, כדכתיב (ויקרא כה) והתנחלתם וכו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:6:2.english: The found item of his Canaanite slave or maidservant is his - For his body is acquired by him permanently, as it is written (Leviticus 25): "And you shall bequeath them," etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:6:3.english: The found item of his wife - The Rabbis instituted [that it belongs] to him because of enmity.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:6:4.hebrew: מציאת עבדו ושפחתו העברים - בגמ' פריך: לא יהא אלא פועל, דאמרינן לעיל (בבא מציעא דף י.) מציאתו לבעל הבית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:6:4.english: The found item of his Hebrew slave or maidservant - In the Gemara, it asks: Let him be no more than a hired laborer, as we said above (Bava Metzia 10a) [that] his found item belongs to the employer.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:7:1.hebrew: מפני מה אמרו מציאת קטן לאביו - בשלמא בתו ואשתו, טעמא מפרש להו במקומן בכתובות; אלא בנו, טעמא מאי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:7:1.english: For what [reason] did they say [that] the found item of a minor [belongs] to his father - Granted, [regarding] his daughter and his wife, their reason is explained in their place in Ketubot; however, [regarding] his son, what is the reason?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:7:2.hebrew: מריצה אצל אביו - הלכך, כשמגביה, לצורך אביו הגביהה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:7:2.english: He runs with it to his father - Therefore, when he lifts [it], he lifted it for his father's sake.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:8:1.hebrew: ילקט בנו אחריו - מותר לבנו של פועל, אם עני הוא, ללקוט אחר אביו לקט הנושר. אבל אם קבל הפועל את השדה למחצה, לשליש ולרביע, עשיר הוא והרי הוא כבעל הבית בשדה זה, ולא ילקט בנו אחריו, לפי שלקט בנו לאביו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:8:1.english: His son may glean after him - It is permitted for the son of a laborer, if he is poor, to glean behind his father the gleanings that fall. However, if the laborer took on the field for a half, a third, or a quarter [of the produce], he is [considered] wealthy and is like a landowner in this field, and his son may not glean after him, because his son's gleanings [belong] to his father.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:8:2.hebrew: בין כך ובין כך כו' - דאם האב עשיר, הבן עני וזוכה לעצמו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 12a:8:2.english: In both this [case] and that [case], etc. - For if the father is wealthy, the son is poor and acquires [them] for himself.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:10:1.hebrew: שמואל טעמא דתנא דידן קאמר - וא"ת: אמאי לא אוקמה בטעמא דידיה, דסבר שמואל דזכי לנפשיה מדאורייתא, ומדרבנן אבוה זכי מיניה משום איבה, וכרבי יוסי? וי"ל, דקטן דקתני במתני' משמע ליה בקטן ממש, ואע"פ שאינו סמוך על שלחנו. ואילו היה זוכה לעצמו מן התורה, לא היה להם לתקן שיזכה אביו, כיון דליכא איבה, שהרי אינו סמוך על שולחנו. אלא ודאי לא זכי לנפשיה כלל אלא לאביו, שבשעת הגבהה מגביה לצורך אביו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:10:1.english: Shmuel is stating the reason of the tanna of our [mishna] - And if you ask: Why did [Shmuel] not establish [the mishna] according to his own reasoning — for Shmuel holds that [a minor] acquires for himself by Torah law, and by Rabbinic law his father acquires from him because of animosity, and in accordance with Rabbi Yosei? And one can answer: For "a minor" that the mishna teaches implies to him an actual minor, even though he is not supported at his [father's] table. And if he were able to acquire for himself by Torah law, [the Sages] would not have enacted that his father acquires [the find], since there is no animosity, for he is not supported at his table. Rather, certainly he does not acquire for himself at all, but rather for his father, for at the time of lifting [it], he lifts [it] for his father's needs.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:1:1.hebrew: חצר משום יד אתרבאי, ולכך כי הוי דומיא דיד — דהיינו כשהוא - בצד חצרו, קונה אפילו בע"כ, או אפילו קטנה כמו בידה. וכשאינה סמוכה לחצרה, דלא הוי דומיא דיד, לא תימא כי היכי דאין לו דין יד הכי נמי אין לו דין שליחות, אלא לא גרע משליחות; ובמידי דזכות, כמו מתנה, קנה — ואפילו אינו עומד בצד חצרו, ואפילו אינה משתמרת. ובמציאה, דאין דעת אחרת מקנה אותה, בעינן משתמרת. ובגט, דחוב הוא לה, אפילו במשתמרת אינה מתגרשת, דלא עדיפא משליחות, דאין חבין לאדם שלא בפניו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:1:1.english: "A courtyard is included due to [its functioning as one's] hand," and therefore when it is similar to a hand — that is, when one is - beside his courtyard, he acquires [with it] even against his will, or even a minor girl [can acquire with it, just as] with her hand. And when she is not near her courtyard, so that it is not similar to a hand, do not say that just as it does not have the law of a hand, so too it does not have the law of agency; rather, it is no less [effective] than agency. Thus, in a matter of benefit, such as a gift, one acquires [it], even if he is not standing beside his courtyard, and even if it is not guarded. But in [the case of] a found object, where there is no other person's intent transferring it [to him], we require [that the courtyard be] guarded. And in [the case of] a bill of divorce, which is detrimental to her, even in a guarded [courtyard] she is not divorced [when not standing beside it], because it is no better than agency, as one cannot act against a person's interests in his absence.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:3:1.hebrew: ויצא בפתח אחר - ל"ג "ואפקריה", דהא חשיב ליה דעת אחרת מקנה אותו, דמייתי ראיה ממתנה; ואי אפקריה, אם כן מיד כשיצא הארנקי מידו היה הפקר, ובשעת זכייה ליכא דעת אחרת. אלא ל"ג "ואפקריה", ולעולם היא שלו עד שיזכה בה אחר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:3:1.english: And it exited through another entrance - We do not read [the words] "and he declared it ownerless," for [the Gemara] considers this [a case of] another person's intent transferring ownership of it, as it brings a proof from [the case of] a gift. And if he had declared it ownerless, then immediately when the purse left his hand it would be ownerless, and at the time of acquisition there would be no other [person's] intent [transferring it]. Rather, we do not read "and he declared it ownerless," and it remains his until another [person] acquires it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:8:1.hebrew: ואמר שמואל הלכה כרבי יוסי - תימה, דבפ' כל הגט (גיטין דף ל. ושם ד"ה כיחידאה) לא בעי שמואל לאוקמי מתניתין ד"המלוה מעות את הכהן ואת הלוי [להיות מפריש עליהן מחלקן]" כרבי יוסי, ד"כיחידאה לא מוקמינן", והכא פסיק הלכה כמותו. וי"ל, דדוקא הכא גבי לקט פסיק כוותיה, מהאי טעמא דמסתמא עניים גופייהו ניחא להו כו'. והא דאוקמי בפרק כל הגט (שם) כרבי יוסי — היינו רבי יוסי דפ' הלוקח עובר פרתו (בכורות דף יח. ושם ד"ה עשו), דאמר: "כל שחליפיו ביד כהן — פטור מן המתנות", ומפרש טעמא בגמ' משום דעשו את שאינו זוכה כזוכה, דהוי דומיא ד"המלוה מעות", דהוו חליפין ביד כהן, דהיינו מעות, ועשו כאילו זכה במעשר עצמו. והא דקרי ליה יחידאה — אע"ג דבבכורות לא פליג אלא ר"מ, מ"מ רבנן דפליגי עליה הכא גבי לקט, כ"ש דפליגי עליה התם גבי מתנות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:8:1.english: And Shmuel says [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - It is astonishing, for in the chapter Kol HaGet (Gittin 30a, and there s.v. keyechida'ah), Shmuel did not want to establish the Mishnah of "One who lends money to a priest or a Levite [to set aside (tithes) for them from their portion]" in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, because "we do not establish [a Mishnah] in accordance with an individual opinion," whereas here he rules the halakha in accordance with him. And one can say that specifically here, regarding gleanings, he rules in accordance with him for this reason: that presumably the poor themselves are amenable [to this], etc. And that which they established [the Mishnah] in the chapter Kol HaGet (ibid.) in accordance with Rabbi Yosei — this refers to Rabbi Yosei of the chapter HaLoke'ach Ubar Parato (Bekhorot 18a, and there s.v. asu), who says: "Anything whose exchange is in the hand of a priest is exempt from the [priestly] gifts," and the Gemara explains the reason: because they treated one who does not acquire as one who acquires — which is similar to "One who lends money," where the exchange is in the hand of the priest, namely the money, and they treated [it] as though he acquired the tithe itself. And [as for] that which it calls him an individual opinion — even though in Bekhorot only Rabbi Meir disagrees [with him], nevertheless, [since] the Rabbis disagree with him here regarding gleanings, all the more so do they disagree with him there regarding [priestly] gifts.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:9:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא דאורייתא - תימה: מנ"ל דלר' יוסי קטן זוכה מן התורה? וכן בסמוך דפריך: "וסבר רבי יוסי מציאת קטן דאורייתא"? ומנ"ל? ודלמא אינה אלא מדרבנן, ואביו לא זכה מיניה כלל, ולהכי מלקט אחריו! וי"ל, דמסתמא לא פליג ר' יוסי אכמה משניות דפרקין, ודפרק חלון (עירובין דף עט: ושם), ודמסכת מעשר שני (פ"ד מ"ד), דמייתי בפרק התקבל (גיטין דף סה. ושם), דלכולהו משניות יד בן כיד אביו. וא"ת: ונימא לעולם זכי לנפשיה מדרבנן, ובתר הכי זכי אבוה מיניה משום איבה, ומשום הכי מלקט? וי"ל, דמדרבנן אין סברא שיתקנו שתי זכיות — שיזכה הבן קודם, ואח"כ יזכה האב ממנו; אלא אי מדרבנן הוא, בשעת זכיית הבן בא לו זכיית האב, משום דבשעת הגבהה לוקחה להריצה לאביו. אלא ודאי זכה לנפשיה מדאורייתא, ואבוה זכה מיניה משום איבה, שסמוך על שלחנו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:9:1.english: Granted, if you say [it is] by Torah law - It is astonishing: from where do we [know] that according to Rabbi Yosei a minor acquires [property] by Torah law? And similarly [in the Gemara] shortly below, where it asks: "And does Rabbi Yosei hold [that] a minor's found object [is his] by Torah law?" — and from where do we [know this]? Perhaps it is only by rabbinic decree, and his father does not acquire [it] from him at all, and therefore he may glean after him! And one can answer that presumably Rabbi Yosei does not disagree with several Mishnayot in our chapter, and in the chapter [entitled] Chalon (Eruvin 79b and there), and in Tractate Ma'aser Sheni (4:4), which [the Gemara] cites in the chapter [entitled] Hamekabel (Gittin 65a and there), [according to] all of which Mishnayot, the hand of a son is like the hand of his father. And if you ask: Let us say that indeed he acquires for himself by rabbinic decree, and afterward his father acquires [it] from him [to prevent] ill will, and therefore he may glean? And one can answer that by rabbinic decree, it is not logical that they would institute two acquisitions — that the son would acquire [it] first, and afterward the father would acquire [it] from him; rather, if it is by rabbinic decree, at the time of the son's acquisition, the father's acquisition takes effect for him, because at the time of lifting [the object], he takes it to run it to his father. Rather, certainly he acquires for himself by Torah law, and his father acquires [it] from him [to prevent] ill will, since he is supported at his [father's] table.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:9:2.hebrew: ואבוה עשיר הוא - לאו דוקא עשיר, אלא כלומר: כיון שיש לו חלק בשדה, חייב בלקט, כדדרשינן לר"א פ"ק דגיטין (דף יב. ושם): "לא תלקט לעני" — להזהיר עני על שלו; ולרבנן נמי, או נפקא להו מקרא אחרינא, או תרתי ש"מ:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 12a:9:2.english: And his father is wealthy - [This does] not specifically [mean] wealthy; rather, it means that since he has a share in the field, he is obligated in [leaving] gleanings, as we expound according to Rabbi Eliezer in the first chapter of Gittin (12a and there): "You shall not glean for the poor" — to warn a poor person concerning his own [field]; and according to the Rabbis as well, either they derive [this] from another verse, or both [laws] are learned from it:
